claim: Once one opponent's board is big enough to kill you in a single attack, stop tapping out for another big Dragon. On your turn, either spend Beast Within or Chaos Warp on their key piece, or keep 3 mana open for Beast Within and 2 for Counterspell. A new 8-drop blocks one creature. It does not stop a swing of 70 power.
evidence: Game 0006, round 8: Lathril had just killed Zuko with a 38-power swing and had about 25 Elves plus Crown of Skemfar. Miirym tapped out for Ancient Silver Dragon, leaving only Haven of the Spirit Dragon untapped, with Beast Within and Counterspell in hand. In round 9 Lathril swung 72 power at it and it died from 28 life, unable to pay {2}{G} for Beast Within on Crown of Skemfar. The pilot's own note: 'never tap out with Lathril's board untouched.'

Game 0042, round 8: at 18 life, the pilot Chaos Warped Laughing Jasper Flint 'which was stealing cards off the top of my library'. Flint's triggers targeted Wilhelt's library, not Miirym's. Next turn, Obeka's Drakuseth killed the Dragon token and dealt 3 to Miirym with its trigger. Then Drakuseth (7), Skyline Despot (5) and Savage Ventmaw (4) left her at -2. Warping Drakuseth would have removed 10 of that damage and saved the token.

Game 0052, round 7 (table turn 26). The pilot was at 11 commander damage from Tidus, whom Herald of Secret Streams made unblockable, and wrote that it would keep Temple plus one Treasure for Rift. It then spent both Treasures on Wrathful Red Dragon and ended with 1 mana open. On turn 28 Tidus hit for 7 (18 commander damage, 10 life), and the pilot noted it could not cast Rift. Tidus finished it on turn 31 with 27 commander damage.

claim: Overload Cyclonic Rift ({6}{U}) in your own main phase, after the go-wide opponent has attacked and tapped out, and before your combat. That bounces every blocker, erases their tokens, and lets your fliers swing into an empty board.
evidence: Game 0007, round 9: Miirym overloaded Rift while all of Lathril's Elves were tapped, which wiped every token. Utvara Hellkite and a token then dealt Zuko exactly lethal, and three attack triggers left Miirym with seven creatures. Lathril died the next turn to a 36-damage swing.

Game 0052, round 8 (table turn 30). The overloaded Rift bounced Zuko's whole board, including Embercleave, and Lulu. Tidus answered with Ripples of Potential from two open lands, and his commander and Herald phased out. Five Dragons hit Tidus for 24 (27 to 3), but his commander returned and killed the pilot the next turn. The pilot had held Rift since round 5 and never spent it on the commander.

claim: Once Miirym is on the battlefield, follow up with Atarka, World Render. Miirym copies Atarka, and each Atarka gives every attacking Dragon double strike, so the 6/6 flier deals 12 commander damage in one swing. Point that damage at the player with no fliers or reach.
evidence: Game 0006, round 6: Atarka was copied by Miirym, Elemental Bond drew two cards, and Miirym hit Lathril (who had no flying or reach) for 6 plus 6, leaving 28 life and 12 commander damage.

claim: If an opponent changes the target of your spell (Redirect Lightning, Deflecting Swat), the spell resolves against the new target only. When Cyclonic Rift gets redirected, the original attacker stays in combat, so plan your blocks and life total for that. Fire Lord Zuko decks in these pods carry target-changing spells, so expect them before you spend Rift on an attacker.
evidence: Game 0032, turn 15: Miirym Rifted Fire Lord Zuko, who was attacking with Embercleave. Zuko's Redirect Lightning moved the Rift onto Yuriko. Miirym bounced Zuko anyway, and the auditor reversed it. Zuko's 12 double-strike damage then counted, putting Miirym at 21 life with 12 commander damage.

claim: Spend Jade Orb of Dragonkind's {G} only on a Dragon creature spell — that is what gives the Dragon an extra +1/+1 counter and hexproof until your next turn — and pay green instants and sorceries from a Forest instead. Get the Orb onto the battlefield early: it is the cheapest way to make the Dragon you most need to keep untargetable on the turn it lands. (Evidence, corrected: on turns 29 and 31 the Orb's {G} was spent on Lathliss and Ureni, each of which entered hexproof until the pilot's next turn and was never targeted, while on turn 33 the Orb's mana went to Beast Within and Miirym was recast with no protection.)
evidence: Game 0062: Jade Orb was in the opening hand and was not cast until round 8 (turn 29). On turn 33 the pilot tapped Jade Orb, Island and Exotic Orchard for Beast Within (which Tidus countered with An Offer You Can't Refuse) while two Forests stood untapped, then recast Miirym for 8 with no protection into a Tidus who had already cast Farewell, Path to Exile and Swords to Plowshares. On turns 29 and 31 the Orb's {G} was spent correctly, on Lathliss and Ureni, and both survived that removal. (Put right by the fact check: The log shows Tidus cast Path to Exile (turn 26) and Farewell (turn 28), but never cast Swords to Plowshares: at turn 25 main1 Tidus's rad-counter trigger milled Swords to Plowshares to the graveyard ('Tidus mills Swords to Plowshares'). The pilot's turn-26 note that Tidus 'has shown Swords to Plowshares' is not borne out by the record; the card only ever went from library to graveyard. Tidus's other interaction that turn was An Offer You Can't Refuse, which countered Beast Within.; The Orb's {G} was indeed spent on Lathliss (turn 29) and Ureni (turn 31), and both ended on the battlefield, but the record shows no opponent removal was ever aimed at either one. After turn 29 Tidus's only interaction was An Offer You Can't Refuse countering Beast Within (turn 33); Farewell and Path to Exile both happened before Lathliss and Ureni entered. Nothing was survived because nothing was pointed at them.)

claim: Miirym is the multiplier, not just another body: any Dragon that enters while she is in the command zone or absent is a single card. After a wrath, recast her the first turn you can pay the commander tax and still spend Jade Orb of Dragonkind's {G} on her, before you deploy Ureni of the Unwritten or another expensive Dragon.
evidence: Game 0062: Tidus's Farewell (turn 28) exiled the whole board. Turn 29, with 9 lands and the Orb still to cast, delaying Miirym for Lathliss was right. Turn 31 was not: 9 lands plus Jade Orb was 10 mana against Miirym's 8, and the pilot spent it on Ganax plus Ureni instead — Ureni's trigger put Ancient Silver Dragon onto the battlefield with Miirym still in the command zone, so it arrived as one body. On turn 33, with Miirym recast first, Ureni's attack trigger found Drakuseth and Miirym immediately made a token copy of it.

claim: Count Scourge of Valkas's own enters trigger. With Miirym out, one Scourge gives three damage triggers — the card's own, the token copy's own, and the card's again when the token enters — each equal to the number of Dragons you control as it resolves. Put the card's own trigger on the stack yourself before you declare an attack lethal, and remember the triggers still resolve off last known information if the Scourge is removed in response.
evidence: Game 0062 turn 26: the real Scourge's own enters trigger was never put on the stack (only Garruk's Uprising, Miirym's copy trigger and Sarkhan's). Tidus then exiled Scourge with Path to Exile, yet the token and Sarkhan-as-Scourge still dealt 7 each to The Wise Mothman from last known values. The missed trigger was added at turn 27 upkeep for 6 damage, taking Mothman from 6 life to 0 — the whole kill rode on a trigger the pilot nearly lost.

claim: On the turn Miirym enters, take Sarkhan, Soul Aflame's copy trigger on Miirym herself rather than on a bigger Dragon: for the rest of that turn every nontoken Dragon that enters makes two token copies. Then cast your cheapest Dragon after her — Scaled Nurturer is a Dragon Druid, so Dragon cost reducers apply to it and Miirym copies it into extra mana creatures. Decline the copy trigger until you have cast the Dragons that need Sarkhan's {1} discount, because he loses it while he is a copy.
evidence: Game 0062 turn 23: Miirym was cast for {G}{U}{R} off Dragonspeaker Shaman and Sarkhan, Sarkhan copied her, and the Scaled Nurturer recast for {0} then made two Nurturer token copies instead of one. Those three Nurturers tapped for Kodama's Reach on turn 26, the turn that killed The Wise Mothman.

claim: Hold Treasures through declare blockers, then spend them all on Lathliss, Dragon Queen's {1}{R}: it pumps every attacking Dragon at once, so blocked Dragons kill their blockers and unblocked ones carry the extra damage. Pumping before blocks are declared only tells the defender how to block. (Evidence, corrected: on turn 33 the pilot had ten Treasures — Ganax's triggers plus two handed over by Tidus's An Offer You Can't Refuse — and after Tidus declared four blockers activated Lathliss five times for +5/+0 on all Dragons, killing Thrummingbird, Luminous Broodmoth, Grateful Apparition and Tidus, Yuna's Guardian, while unblocked Ganax and Ureni dealt 8 and 13 to take Tidus from 29 to 8.)
evidence: Game 0062 turn 33: Ganax's Treasures accumulated to ten; after Tidus declared four blockers the pilot activated Lathliss five times for +5/+0 on all Dragons, killing Thrummingbird, Luminous Broodmoth, Grateful Apparition and Tidus, Yuna's Guardian, while unblocked Ganax and Ureni dealt 8 and 13 to take Tidus from 29 to 8. (Put right by the fact check: Ten Treasures were sacrificed for the five Lathliss activations, but two of them were not Ganax's: at turn 33 main1 Tidus's An Offer You Can't Refuse countered Beast Within and 'Tidus creates 2 Treasure token(s) for Miirym'. The rest came from Ganax's triggers (one per Dragon entering, tokens included) across turns 31 and 33, with one Ganax Treasure spent on Miirym's casting cost.)
